title: 15 Home Business Ideas for Ladies in India 2026
summary: Low cost ideas for housewives, what each needs, how to start from home, and government schemes to check.
body_markdown:
The best home business ideas for ladies in India need little money and fit around family time: selling financial products on commission, a tiffin service, tailoring, home salon work, and online tutoring. Pick one that uses a skill you already have, start with neighbours and relatives, and grow by word of mouth. If you would rather find a job than run a business, see[work from home jobs for housewives](https://gromo.in/blog/work-from-home-jobs-for-housewives/) .


Below are 15 home business ideas for women with what each costs, the skills it needs and the steps to start. Earnings depend on your time and customers, so we make no income promises. Where an idea needs a licence, we say so.


# Idea Starting cost Skills needed Best for


1 Selling Financial Products With GroMo None Basic phone use; free training in the app Anyone 18 or older


2 Home Tiffin Service Low Cooking, punctuality Good home cooks


3 Tailoring and Stitching Medium Stitching Women who know sewing


4 Home Salon and Beauty Services Medium Beauty training Trained beauticians


5 Online Tutoring and Home Tuition Very low Subject knowledge, patience Educated homemakers


6 Pickles, Papad and Homemade Food Low Recipes, packaging Women known for their cooking


7 Baking and Cakes Low Baking, decoration Hobby bakers


8 Reselling Sarees and Fashion Low Selling, trust Women with a big social circle


9 Handmade Crafts and Candles Low Craft skill Creative women


10 Freelance Writing or Translation Very low Good language skills Women comfortable with Hindi and English


11 Online Selling on Marketplaces Low Basic packing and listing Women with a product to sell


12 Day Care or Baby Sitting Low Childcare experience, safe home Experienced mothers


13 Yoga or Fitness Classes Low Certification Trained instructors


14 Social Media Management for Local Shops Very low Instagram, Canva Young women with digital skills


15 Mehendi and Event Decoration Very low Mehendi or decoration skill Artistic women


Starting-cost labels are our own rough estimates: None, Very low, Low and Medium. Actual costs depend on your city and setup.


How this list is ranked: GroMo comes first because it needs no money, no stock and no shop. The rest follow the ideas that keep appearing in the top-ranking Indian guides for this search, with the lowest-cost, easiest-to-start ideas placed higher.


## 1. Selling Financial Products With GroMo: Bank-paid commissions, no stock


**Starting cost:** None | **Skills:** Basic phone use; free training in the app | **Best for:** Anyone 18 or older


Selling financial products with GroMo tops this list because it costs nothing to start and needs only a smartphone. GroMo is a free app where you help people apply for credit cards, savings accounts, loans and demat accounts from partner banks, and you earn a commission when the application is approved. On GroMo, credit cards pay up to ₹2,000, savings accounts up to ₹1,000, demat accounts up to ₹450, and personal loans up to 4.5% of the loan amount (GroMo catalogue, retrieved 2026-11-06). You can work from home in your free hours with no targets, and women in your circle who need a first bank account or card are often glad to get help from someone they trust. The pay is commission only, with no fixed salary, and only approved applications earn; you must be 18 or older.


How to start:


1. Download the GroMo app and register free with your phone number.
2. Finish the one-time verification and the free in-app training.
3. Share a product link with someone who genuinely needs it, then track the application in the app.


## 2. Home Tiffin Service: Home-cooked meals for offices and PGs


**Starting cost:** Low | **Skills:** Cooking, punctuality | **Best for:** Good home cooks


A tiffin service is listed in nearly every guide for housewives because working people and PG students want home-style food. Daily orders make income regular, and FSSAI registration starts at about ₹100 a year (IncorpX, retrieved 2026-11-06).


How to start:


1. Cook one menu for five customers as a trial.
2. Get FSSAI registration.
3. Take monthly orders through WhatsApp.


## 3. Tailoring and Stitching: Blouses, alterations, kids' wear


**Starting cost:** Medium | **Skills:** Stitching | **Best for:** Women who know sewing


Tailoring from home has steady demand, particularly around weddings and festivals. A sewing machine is the main cost, and alteration jobs are an easy way to win your first customers.


How to start:


1. Start with alterations for neighbours.
2. Show finished blouses on WhatsApp Status.
3. Add festive and bridal work.


## 4. Home Salon and Beauty Services: Parlour work at home


**Starting cost:** Medium | **Skills:** Beauty training | **Best for:** Trained beauticians


Home salon services appear on Tata Capital's list of home business ideas for women. You save on rent, and regular clients return every month, but hygiene and basic training matter from day one.


How to start:


1. Complete basic training if you need it.
2. Start with services for neighbours.
3. Add bridal and festive packages later.


## 5. Online Tutoring and Home Tuition: Teach children from home


**Starting cost:** Very low | **Skills:** Subject knowledge, patience | **Best for:** Educated homemakers


Tuition fits family life because classes happen in fixed after-school hours. Lendingkart lists online tutoring among the most profitable options for women, and you can start in your own neighbourhood before going online.


How to start:


1. Pick classes and subjects you can teach.
2. Start with two or three local children.
3. Move some batches online.


## 6. Pickles, Papad and Homemade Food: Small batches, big festive demand


**Starting cost:** Low | **Skills:** Recipes, packaging | **Best for:** Women known for their cooking


Homemade food products sell well during festivals and to people living away from home. Good packaging and hygiene make a big difference, and you need FSSAI registration before selling regularly.


How to start:


1. Make one small batch and get feedback.
2. Get FSSAI registration and simple labels.
3. Sell locally, then on WhatsApp and online.


## 7. Baking and Cakes: Birthday and festive orders


**Starting cost:** Low | **Skills:** Baking, decoration | **Best for:** Hobby bakers


Home baking grows through birthdays and festivals, and one good cake often brings the next order. An oven is the main cost if you don't already have one, and FSSAI registration applies here too.


How to start:


1. Bake for friends and take clear photos.
2. Get FSSAI registration.
3. Take pre-orders only, so nothing goes to waste.


## 8. Reselling Sarees and Fashion: Sell through WhatsApp groups


**Starting cost:** Low | **Skills:** Selling, trust | **Best for:** Women with a big social circle


Reselling sarees, suits and jewellery is popular because you can start from your phone. Show products from a supplier, take the payment and then place the order, so you aren't left holding stock.


How to start:


1. Find a reliable supplier.
2. Share products on WhatsApp Status.
3. Order only after the customer pays.


## 9. Handmade Crafts and Candles: Gifts and festive items


**Starting cost:** Low | **Skills:** Craft skill | **Best for:** Creative women


Handmade candles, jewellery and gift items sell well around Diwali and weddings. Selling takes effort, so local fairs, society groups and Instagram are the best places to begin.


How to start:


1. Make a small festive batch.
2. Sell at society fairs and to friends.
3. Open an Instagram page with good photos.


## 10. Freelance Writing or Translation: Earn from home with words


**Starting cost:** Very low | **Skills:** Good language skills | **Best for:** Women comfortable with Hindi and English


Freelance writing and translation can be done during quiet hours with just a phone or laptop. Hindi writers are in demand, so strong Hindi is a real advantage, and samples matter more than certificates.


How to start:


1. Write three samples.
2. Create a profile on a freelancing site.
3. Start with small jobs to build reviews.


## 11. Online Selling on Marketplaces: Reach customers beyond your area


**Starting cost:** Low | **Skills:** Basic packing and listing | **Best for:** Women with a product to sell


Online selling lets you reach customers beyond your neighbourhood. Marketplace rules, fees and returns take some learning, so try it after your product already sells well locally.


How to start:


1. Pick a product with proven local demand.
2. Register as a seller and read the fees.
3. Start with a few listings.


## 12. Day Care or Baby Sitting: High trust, regular income


**Starting cost:** Low | **Skills:** Childcare experience, safe home | **Best for:** Experienced mothers


Home day care serves working parents nearby and brings steady monthly income. Safety is everything here, so keep the group small, check local rules, and give parents regular updates.


How to start:


1. Check local rules for childcare.
2. Start with one or two children you know.
3. Add more only as you can manage safely.


## 13. Yoga or Fitness Classes: Women-only batches


**Starting cost:** Low | **Skills:** Certification | **Best for:** Trained instructors


Women-only yoga and fitness batches are popular in housing societies, where many women prefer training close to home. A certification builds trust, and an open terrace or hall can be enough to begin.


How to start:


1. Get certified if you aren't already.
2. Start a small morning batch in your society.
3. Offer monthly plans.


## 14. Social Media Management for Local Shops: Digital work from home


**Starting cost:** Very low | **Skills:** Instagram, Canva | **Best for:** Young women with digital skills


Social media management means running Instagram pages for local shops and boutiques. You can do it in free hours from a phone, and one good example page can bring more clients.


How to start:


1. Build one sample page.
2. Pitch to three local shops.
3. Charge a monthly fee after a trial.


## 15. Mehendi and Event Decoration: Seasonal, high-demand skills


**Starting cost:** Very low | **Skills:** Mehendi or decoration skill | **Best for:** Artistic women


Mehendi and small event decoration bring strong seasonal demand during weddings and festivals. Income is uneven through the year, so many women pair it with a steadier idea from this list.


How to start:


1. Practise designs and photograph your work.
2. Share them in local and society groups.
3. Fix package prices before the festive season.


## How Much Does GroMo Pay for Each Product?


Product on GroMo Pays partners up to


SBI Credit Card ₹2,000 per approved card


HDFC Secured Credit Card ₹1,750 per approved card


Axis Saving Account ₹1,000 per account


Digi Credit Personal Loan 4.5% of the loan amount


Kotak 811 Super Account ₹600 per account


Kotak Securities Demat Account ₹450 per account


The SBI Credit Card pays partners up to ₹2,000 per approved card (GroMo catalogue, retrieved 2026-11-06). Commission is paid only on approval.


The Axis Saving Account pays up to ₹1,000 per successful account (GroMo catalogue, retrieved 2026-11-06). Many other products pay less.


The Digi Credit Personal Loan pays up to 4.5% of the loan amount, and most other lenders pay less (GroMo catalogue, retrieved 2026-11-06). Check the live payout in the app.


## Which home business is best for housewives with no money?


Selling financial products on commission, home tuition, freelance writing and social media management are the best home businesses with no money, because they need no stock. A phone and your time are enough. If you have a small budget, a tiffin service or tailoring can bring more regular income. More ideas are in our guide to[female business ideas](https://gromo.in/blog/female-business-ideas/) .


## Which government schemes can help women start a business?


Schemes that guides commonly mention for women include MUDRA loans, Stand-Up India, Udyogini and Annapurna (Tata Capital and SMFG India Credit, retrieved 2026-11-06). Rules, limits and availability change and can vary by state, so check the official website or your bank before you apply. Be careful of agents who ask for a fee to get you a government loan.


## How do you find your first customers from home?


Your first customers will usually be neighbours, relatives and society groups, because they already trust you. Share your work on WhatsApp Status, ask happy customers for a recommendation, and join local groups. For help talking to people about what you sell, read[how to convince a customer](https://gromo.in/blog/how-to-convince-customer/) .


**GroMo** is a free app where partners help customers apply for credit cards, loans, savings accounts and demat accounts from partner banks, and earn a commission on approval.


## FAQ: Home Business Ideas for Ladies


### Which is the best home business for ladies?


That depends on your skills. Selling financial products with GroMo needs no money, while tiffin services, tailoring and home tuition suit women with those skills and bring regular customers.


### Which home business can a housewife start with no investment?


Selling financial products on commission, home tuition, freelance writing and social media management can all start with almost no money.


### Can a housewife use GroMo?


Yes, if you're 18 or older. Joining and training are free, and you need no shop, stock or targets. You earn when a customer's application is approved.


### Do I need a licence to sell food from home?


Yes, food businesses need FSSAI registration, even small ones run from home. Basic registration is low cost.


### How do I avoid work from home scams?


Never pay a registration fee, buy a starter kit from an unknown company, or share your OTP. Genuine work pays you, and it doesn't ask you to pay first.


### Can women get a government loan for a home business?


Schemes such as MUDRA and Stand-Up India exist, but rules vary. Apply through a bank or the official website, not through an agent who asks for a fee.


GroMo (Vitrak Technologies Pvt Ltd) is a distribution platform. GroMo isn't a bank, NBFC, insurer or investment adviser. All products are offered by their respective RBI, IRDAI or SEBI-regulated providers.


Partner earnings depend on effort, product mix and customer eligibility. Any figures shown are illustrative. They aren't typical and aren't promised.


Sources: Top-ranking guides checked: Tata Capital, SMFG India Credit, Lendingkart and Zenind, retrieved 2026-11-06. GroMo product catalogue, commission rates by product, retrieved 2026-11-06.


## Disclaimer


GroMo doesn't promise any level of income. Commissions are set by partner banks, vary by product and campaign, and are paid only on approved applications; check the live commission in the GroMo app. Starting-cost labels are our own rough estimates, and any pay figures from other sites or job listings are what those sources state, not a guarantee. GroMo is available only to users aged 18 and above. Everything above is general information, not financial, legal or career advice.
